meta.description: Intra-space directed edges connecting nodes within Space A (clinical-to-clinical) and within Space B (concept-to-concept). Complements edges.json inside a unified directed graph.
meta.relation_types: See ontology.json. Uses PRECEDES, ILLUSTRATES, CONTRADICTS, and NUANCES.
meta.note_on_PRECEDES: PRECEDES encodes narrative-causal progression in Space A or logical-conceptual derivation in Space B. It applies exclusively to intra-space edges.

space_A.justification: The compulsive muttering symptom in the flat (argo_03) directly motivates the decision to adopt a dog (argo_05). Clara links them explicitly: 'That was when I told myself.' Direct causal progression within the narrative.
The spillover of muttering into public streets and the shame of disguising it behind unplugged earphones (argo_04) mark the tipping point immediately preceding the decision to get a dog (argo_05).
Walter's death from winter pneumonia at home (argo_12) sets the stage for the intimate scene of the three passing together through his final night (argo_13). Direct temporal and narrative continuity.
Walter's death (argo_12) triggers the cascade of secondary losses: underselling the Bristol flat, failed reconciliation with Julian, and relocation to Dartmoor (argo_14).
Moss's death from poisoned meat baits (argo_18) forms the concrete empirical precedent behind the neighbour's blunt warning and Clara's decision to restrict Argo (argo_22).
The neighbour's warning and the decision to restrict Argo's movement (argo_22) directly produce the ongoing daily practice of walking him exclusively on a long lead (argo_23).
The practical restriction imposed after the neighbour's threat (argo_22) leads Clara to formulate the explicit dilemma between freedom and protection (argo_25).
Daily caregiving confinement with frail Walter in the Bristol flat (argo_01) establishes the isolating conditions under which the muttering symptom emerges (argo_03).
Argo's nocturnal alerting whenever Walter stirs (argo_09) leads directly to Clara's interpretive synthesis: 'there were two of us now: Argo and I' (argo_10).

Clara's rationalized decision to guard Argo against rural hazards (argo_25) immediately gives way to the admission that tethering him serves her own emotional survival as 'the only thing left of a life that is gone' (argo_26).

Recognizing Argo as the sole remnant of her vanished Bristol life (argo_26) unfolds into the explicit statement of his ongoing psychic role: sustaining mental stability, mediating grief, and preventing compulsive muttering (argo_27).
Confronting how deeply Argo stabilizes her own mourning (argo_27) immediately precipitates ethical guilt over whether keeping him tethered is fair to him: 'I feel I am sacrificing him' (argo_28).

Links the onset of compulsive muttering in 2019 (argo_03) to Argo's enduring role five years later as 'the cure that keeps me from muttering to myself' (argo_27), demonstrating structural continuity of symptom regulation.

The cumulative losses of 2019 (confinement, breakup with Julian, family pressure in argo_02) recur structurally in the post-bereavement losses of 2022 (undersold flat, failed reconciliation with Julian, displacement in argo_14).

Clara's inaugural promise to lead Argo across wide, unknown horizons and surpass Odysseus (argo_07) stands in sharp contradiction with her present guilt over confining him to a long lead as a humanized house-dog (argo_28).

space_B.justification: Freud's inaugural definition of mourning and melancholia as divergent responses to loss (freud_01) prepares the decisive structural distinction between an impoverished world and an impoverished ego (freud_04).

Distinguishing ego-impoverishment from world-impoverishment (freud_04) requires explaining the metapsychological mechanism behind ego depletion: narcissistic identification whereby 'the shadow of the object fell upon the ego' (freud_10).
Piecemeal withdrawal of libido under reality-testing (freud_05) leads to the classical outcome of completed mourning: an ego that is 'free and uninhibited again' (freud_06).

Unconscious object-loss—knowing whom one lost, but not what was lost in them (freud_07)—drives the enigmatic lowering of self-regard and retroactive self-reproach characteristic of melancholia (freud_08).
Clinical observation that self-reproaches are transposed accusations against a loved object (freud_09) is explained structurally by narcissistic identification with the abandoned object (freud_10).

Introjection of the abandoned object into the ego (freud_10) transforms external relational conflict into an internal cleavage between the ego's critical agency and the ego altered by identification (freud_11).
Ambivalence as a precondition of melancholia (freud_13) unleashes retroflected sadism (freud_14): while love retreats into identification, hate attacks the substitutive introjected object.
Sadistic self-torment (freud_14) reaches its extreme limit in melancholic suicide, where the ego treats itself as the hated, overpowering object (freud_15).

Specifies the structural contrast between world-impoverishment and ego-impoverishment (freud_04) in epistemic terms: conscious loss in mourning versus unconscious dimension of loss in melancholia (freud_07).
While completed mourning leaves the ego free (freud_06), Freud nuances that melancholia too can pass off after time has elapsed, even though it behaves economically like an 'open wound' (freud_16).

Winnicott's living transitional object (theory_05) and Kohut's selfobject (theory_06) form a developmental-metapsychological progression from sensorimotor anxiety buffering to structural self-cohesion.
Bowlby's secure base and safe haven (theory_07) substantiate from evolutionary attachment theory the stabilizing functions Kohut describes intrapsychically via the selfobject (theory_06).
Social non-recognition in disenfranchised grief (theory_11) produces secondary neurotic guilt, public shame, and obstructed mourning (theory_12).
Because genuine bereavement opens a hole in the Real tearing the Imaginary register (theory_08), the lost relational anchor is strictly non-substitutable and non-fungible (theory_09).

Freud's thesis of pure, unambivalent affection toward dogs (theory_02) is directly contradicted by Marie Bonaparte's demonstration of irreducible ambivalence and narcissistic control in animal guardianship (theory_03).
Establishing adaptive continuing bonds through internalization (theory_15) relies operationally on Symbolic rituals and thresholds capable of bordering loss (theory_16).
When disenfranchisement blocks symbolic mourning work (theory_12), unelaborated distress is inscribed somatically as autonomic hyperarousal, insomnia, and loss of appetite (theory_13).
